details:
I'm struggling to exactly phrase what I'm referring to with this so bear with me.

After doing a clean install of Windows I noticed that there were updates for some packages in my project that the Creator Companion did not notify me about.

Upon further inspection it dawned on me that perhaps the VRCCC does not check for updates to packages unless you've explicitly subscribed to them, even if the package is in a project that you have added to it. It will at least identify contained packages as VRCCC packages, but it cannot check for updates to them I asssume because it doesn't actually know where they came from. It also incorrectly reports the current version as latest which can be deceiving.

Now this is no big deal for me because I caught it and corrected it by just going and subscribing to the things I need to be subscribed to again and I can make a mental note to do this anytime I reinstall or change machines from now on.

However I can see this being a potential problem in situations where Person A hands off a project to Person B and Person B is not subscribed to the same things as Person A so they do not get notified about updates to those packages and may continue to work on it with obsolete packages unwittingly because they assumed the VRCCC would handle update checking. It's also going to be a problem if someone uses multiple machines to work on their projects and VRCCC subscriptions are not consistent across those machines.

My suggestion is that the VRCCC should have a way of determining where a VRCCC package was sourced from even if you've never subscribed to it yourself. That way it can check for updates for included packages no matter what.

I have some ideas of how that would work where it would require VRCCC supporting this functionality and then it's up to package developers to include an identifier file to their packages. That or perhaps the VRCCC can simply generate this file and add it to the package directory upon first import. It should probably prompt the user if any strange conflicts are found.

If you want to be extra with keeping it consensual and informative, maybe upon adding a project that contains unsubscribed repos it can throw a prompt saying something along the lines of "This project contains packages you are not currently subscribed to, would you like to subscribe to them?" where if they choose "Yes" it adds those repos, but if they choose "No" it does nothing and from there on out the VRCCC will only display the current version of the package and in the latest version column it just says "Not Subscribed" or something similar, but if they click on it it will prompt them to add the repo again, in case they change their mind later. 

But I won't play backseat dev here. You get the gist of what I'm saying - that I think VRCCC packages should have some way of telling the VRCCC where they came from so that the VRCCC can check for updates to packages contained in a project without the user needing to be explicitly subscribed to those sources.

I noticed this issue due to a reinstall of Windows but I can imagine it also being an issue for people who transfer projects between machines or share projects, which I understand that last scenario is probably not a supported use case anyway for the obvious security concerns that project sharing entails, but still, wanted to at least toss this out there as a suggestion.

There's also the chance that it's already supposed to do something like this, in which case I guess this becomes a bug report, lol.

Thanks.
title: The Creator Companion should be able to check for updates to VRCCC packages contained in a project even if the current user is not subscribed to the source repo.
